title: 70% of Japanese Think They're Safe from Online Scams
paragraphs: A new survey in Japan has found that even though online scams are on the rise, almost three-quarters of people don't think they'd ever fall victim to one.
In July, Japanese internet company LINE Yahoo surveyed over 1,000 people in Japan about their awareness of online scams. The survey participants were men and women aged between 18 and 69.
About 40% of the survey participants said they were aware of investment scams on social media sites, while 70% said they were aware of scams by people pretending to be the police.
About half of the participants also said they had experienced something that could have been the start of a scam, such as emails about investments from people or organizations they didn't know.

But when asked if they thought they could be scammed, more than 70% said they didn't think so. The survey also found that older people were more likely to believe that they couldn't be fooled by a scam.

However, previous data suggests that people are too confident in their ability to spot scams. A 2018 survey by Japan's National Police Agency found that 78% of scam victims believed they couldn't be scammed before it happened to them.

Recent data from the National Police Agency shows that online scams are actually increasing. In 2025, there were almost 10,000 cases of investment-type fraud on social media sites in Japan, and almost 11,000 cases of fraud by fake police.
